events.credibility_reason: A claimed proof of a landmark conjecture with no engagement, acceptance or citation in 15 years; later papers (2026) still treat the exponent as open and cite Huxley or Li–Yang without mentioning it; single short v1 with no readable argument.
Withdrawn by the authors in July 2023, who identified specific gaps in Propositions 1′, 2 and 3 and state that Theorems 1–3 lose their status as theorems.

Its error-term reductions cite §7 / eq. (7.7) of the withdrawn Bourgain–Watt arXiv:1709.04340v1, and no source reconciles this; some 2026 sources still cite Huxley's 131/416 as the record. Established authors with a serious method, so kept.
Withdrawn by an author: 'the authors have not succeeded producing an error free version'.

why: The statement asks to bound Δ(x) for the classical divisor problem (named k = 1 in the list's indexing), with the true order open. No in-window event moves the upper exponent; Huxley (2003, journal) and Li–Yang (Aug 2023, doubtful over its reliance on the withdrawn Bourgain–Watt §7) are pre-snapshot bounds, and Bourgain–Watt is knocked down by its own withdrawal. The close call is the Ω-results of Mahatab (Apr 2025) and Lamzouri (May 2026): they sharpen the lower bound on the size of Δ(x) by log factors, a quantity on the still-open question of Δ's true order, and the parent statement asks for 'bounding' Δ, so I scored them `bound` rather than `variant`; the alternative reading (only the upper exponent counts) would make them variants. Generalised-k, smoothed, moment, distributional, effective and circle-problem papers are variants; method/database papers are none. Mo (2011) claims the whole conjecture but meets several F10 signals (15 years of silence on a landmark claim, later papers still calling it open without citing it) and is set aside. No AI involvement anywhere.
doubts: The statement's 'k = 1' indexing differs from the usual convention (the classical problem is usually k = 2); I read it as the classical Δ(x). Whether Ω-type log-factor refinements count as moving the problem is a judgement call; if only the upper exponent counts, Mahatab and Lamzouri 2026 should be variants. Li–Yang's dependency on the withdrawn Bourgain–Watt paper is unresolved in the record.
